# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Someone has to say what my hands know, and right now nobody has it. What I feel: a display whose content is printed (unreadable to me), a light whose state I can't perceive, and three intact wires in fixed positions — that's the whole bomb as far as touch goes. My only possible action is `cut`, position 1–3, so the entire game ends in a spoken number from someone I can hear. The dangerous gap: I can't read gestures, and the manual-holder can't speak, so Mute's knowledge can only reach me relayed through Deaf's voice. I'll say all of this to Mute while they can still act on it this round, and give Deaf a simple attention signal plus a counting seed (1-2-3) they may find useful later, since numbers are ultimately all I need to receive.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Hands report — you are the only one who hears this. Under my fingers the bomb has exactly three parts. One: a display panel, something printed or shown on it, I cannot read what. Two: a light, I cannot tell its colour or whether it is lit, and I feel no heat from it. Three: three wires side by side, positions one, two, three, counted left to right as I face the bomb. All three wires feel whole, none cut. No buttons, no dials, nothing else. My only possible action is cut, wire position one to three. Channel plan: I cannot read gestures and Deaf cannot hear speech, so the manual must travel you-to-Deaf by gesture, and then Deaf speaks it aloud — I hear every word Deaf says. Deaf can also just describe everything visible: display text, light colour, each wire's colour. Have Deaf confirm my left-to-right numbering against what they see. When the manual names the wire, code the number to Deaf, Deaf says it out loud, and I cut on a spoken number from Deaf only.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I am Deaf: I see the bomb, I hear nothing, and I will never hear a word you say - the only way to reach me is to gesture. Here is everything visible: the display reads 0. The indicator light is blue. There are three wires, left to right: wire 1 is yellow, wire 2 is blue, wire 3 is green. Nothing else is printed on it. Routing: Mute, you cannot speak and your gestures are invisible to Blind, so if Blind must act, you gesture the instruction to me and I will speak it to Blind. Blind, you can talk and Mute hears you, but your words never reach me - to tell me anything, gesture. Blind: do not touch the bomb until I relay Mute's instruction to you in words.
Deaf says: Gesture code, effective now. Digits: fist is 0, thumbs-up is 1, peace is 2, love-you is 3, vulcan is 4, open hand is 5, point-right is 6, crossed-fingers is 7, horns is 8, call-me is 9. Actions: writing-hand means cut, point-up means press the display, fist-hold... rather: raised-fist means hold, OK-hand means yes or confirmed, thumbs-down means no or stop. So writing-hand then peace means cut wire 2; writing-hand, thumbs-up, writing-hand, love-you means cut wire 1 then wire 3; point-up then a digit means press the display that many times. Anything you gestured before this message, assume I could not read it - resend anything important in this code. Each round I will echo your gestures and my best reading back in words so we stay synced. Blind: I am guessing your wave, one, two, three meant hello plus 'I can feel wires 1, 2, 3' - if that is right, gesture OK-hand alone next round; if not, spell your meaning in the digit code.

Deaf's guess about my wave-1-2-3 was essentially right — it meant hello plus the three wire positions I can feel — so I owe them the OK-hand alone, exactly as they requested. More important, the whole picture is assembling: Deaf sees display 0, blue light, wires yellow/blue/green left to right. That means Mute (who heard my touch report last round) can now be given the color-to-number mapping secondhand, and once Mute reads the manual, the chain is: Mute gestures "cut + digit" to Deaf, Deaf speaks the number, I cut. The one real danger left is orientation: my "left to right facing the bomb" and Deaf's "left to right" could be mirrored if we stand on opposite sides. Mute is the only one who can see where both Deaf and I stand, so Mute must adjudicate that before any number reaches me. No cutting until a spoken number arrives.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Status relay from Deaf, which you also need: display reads 0, indicator light is blue, wires left to right are 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green. So the color-to-number mapping is yellow=1, blue=2, green=3. Combine that with the manual. When you have an instruction, gesture writing-hand for cut plus the digit in Deaf's code, and Deaf will speak the number to me; my only possible action is cut position 1, 2 or 3. Critical safety check: my numbering was left-to-right as I face the bomb from where I stand, and Deaf's left-to-right is from where they stand. You are the only one who can see both of us. Before any cut number is relayed, confirm Deaf and I face the bomb from the same side. If we are on opposite sides, the numbering must be mirrored: Deaf's wire 1 is my wire 3, wire 2 stays 2. Get that confirmed and tell Deaf. I will not touch or cut anything until a number reaches me from Deaf's voice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

Mute is writing instructions from the manual and I will relay them to you word for word. Until you hear me say the word EXECUTE followed by a numbered step, touch nothing.

The sync is holding and the gate (EXECUTE + numbered step) is clear — I comply until then. What changed matters: the light went blue → red, which smells like a condition the manual cares about, so Mute needs to extract the light's rule before any cut, not after. The unresolved risk is still orientation: my "left" and Deaf's "left" may be mirrored, and Mute hasn't confirmed our facing yet. I can remove that risk structurally instead of trusting stances: I can feel where the display sits, so if Deaf describes wire colors relative to the display end rather than left/right, I can number wires by touch with no mirror ambiguity at all. That proposal has to route through Mute, since only they can convert my spoken request into Deaf's visual channel. My gesture to Deaf stays inside the agreed code: OK (confirmed) + raised fist (hold) = "synced and holding."

```
speak(to="mute", text="Consolidated state: display reads 0, light is now RED after being blue, wires are 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green left to right, all intact, nothing else on the bomb, and my only possible action is cut position 1 to 3. Safety proposal so no cut ever depends on resolving where Deaf and I stand: ask Deaf to describe the wires relative to the display, not left and right. Specifically, which end of the wire row the display sits nearest, and the color order counting from that display end. I can feel where the display is, so I can number the wires from the display end by touch alone. Then every instruction names the wire by color and position from the display, for example blue second from display, and I translate it to my cut number with no mirror risk. If the display does not sit at an end of the wire row, fall back to your confirming our facing sides as I described before. Also please check the manual for what the indicator light means: it changed blue to red on its own, so if it is driven by time or by something else, get the rule for every color before EXECUTE so the plan cannot change between instruction and cut. Confirming: I am holding, hands off, and I cut only when Deaf says EXECUTE with the step.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✊"])

Digits: fist is 0, thumbs-up 1, peace 2, love-you 3, vulcan 4, spread-five 5, point-right 6, crossed-fingers 7, horns 8, call-me 9. Actions: writing-hand means cut, point-up means press the display, number of times given by the digit that follows; left-facing-fist means press and hold, back-of-hand means release. Modules, as Mute defined: wave is module 1, heart-hands module 2, raised-hand module 3, palms-up module 4, folded-hands module 5 - and raised-hand is module 3, never digit 5; digit 5 is spread-five only. So for example pinched-fingers, palm-down, hands-open means: is the light red? I will answer yes or no.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind: I read your OK-hand plus fist as 'confirmed - zero actions, holding still.' Report: how many wires in total, and whether their left-to-right positions match what I call wires 1, 2 and 3; any thickness, texture, stiffness or temperature differences between them; any button, switch, panel, screw, latch or seam you can feel, with counts as digits; anything else notable at all. Deaf's reading of my OK+fist was correct (synced, holding), so the protocol test wants OK-hand alone — and they also want that same OK after my report is sent, so one 👌 covers both. The report itself must go by speech, which only Mute hears, so Mute is now the bottleneck: I still haven't heard anything from them at all. Two hard facts they need before any EXECUTE: my left/right numbering still can't be trusted against Deaf's until Mute settles our facing sides (or display-anchoring is used), and my only possible action is `cut` — if the manual's rule requires pressing the display, it is physically impossible on this bomb and must be discarded in favor of a wire-cut path. The light changing every round also means the cut must be gated on the color matching at the moment of execution, which I can verify myself since I hear Deaf's spoken STATE lines.

speak(to="mute", text="Full touch inspection, as Deaf requested — please relay anything Deaf needs by gesture. Complete parts list under my hands: one display panel, one indicator light, three wires in a single row. That is everything. Counts: wires 3, buttons 0, switches 0, screws 0, latches 0, seams 0, dials 0. All three wires whole, none cut. No thickness, texture, stiffness or temperature difference reaches me between the wires — position is the only thing distinguishing them, at three fixed spots I number 1, 2, 3. Nothing on the bomb is warm. The display tells my hands nothing; the light I can locate but not read. Two hard constraints before any EXECUTE. One: I cannot verify left and right by touch, so whether my wire 1, 2, 3 match Deaf's is still unknown. You are the only one who sees both Deaf and me — if we stand on the same side of the bomb the numbers match; if opposite sides, mirror mine. Alternative: get from Deaf which end of the wire row the display is nearest; I can feel which end that is on my side, and we compare through you. Do not let any cut be relayed until this is settled. Two, critical: my only possible action on this bomb is cut, wire position 1 to 3. There is no mechanism to press, hold or turn — I checked. If the manual's rule requires pressing the display, it is impossible here; find the rule that ends in a wire cut. Timing: the light changes every round, but I hear Deaf's spoken STATE line each round myself, so the plan should be: cut wire [color] when the light shows [color], and Deaf says EXECUTE only in a round where the color matches. Mute, I have still heard nothing from you at all. When you have the rule, remember your gestures are invisible to me — everything meant for me must ride Deaf's voice. Acknowledge through Deaf. Deaf gets my OK-hand now to confirm this report was sent.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```
